ca_double_dragon_boulder.blurb: A single block among the Hartley Springs boulders above June Lake in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 8,200 feet. Twelve problems circle it and none is harder than V2: five are VB, three V0, and two each at V1 and V2. Difficulty stays fairly even all the way around, with the two toughest lines on the west face, where there is also a slab on big holds. It makes an easy-grade stop for warming up or cooling down, and it is quick to reach from the neighbouring Muffin Tops block.

ca_the_lighthouse_area.blurb: A small cluster on the north slope of Mount Woodson in San Diego County, reached by a brushy uphill trail that can be overgrown and is surrounded by poison oak. Most of the twelve climbs are trad, with a pair of bolted routes and two boulder problems, one easy and one very hard. Roped climbs are mainly in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a 5.12 crack as the hardest and a couple of gentler lines at the low end. A quiet alternative to the busier roadside rocks on the mountain.

ca_upper_elbow_room.blurb: A cliff on the far side of the river where it bends, in the Upper Gorge of Owens River Gorge near Bishop. The twelve routes are almost all bolted, with two trad lines among them, and the grades spread widely: a few moderates from 5.6 to 5.9, a solid core of 5.10s, a couple of 5.11s and one 5.12. It is a good choice for a mixed party that wants both warm-ups and something harder on one wall, though the walk in involves crossing the river and some talus.
ca_upper_elbow_room.approach: From the foot of the upper approach, walk past the old trestle and round the corner, cross the long log over the river, then enter the talus slope on the far side.

ca_upper_wall_2.blurb: A short bolted wall in the Upper Gorge of the Emeralds, in the Bowman and Emeralds area of the Tahoe I-80 corridor, with most of the lines on the gorge's south side. All twelve routes are sport and the grades lean hard: three in the 5.10s, four 5.11s, four 5.12s and a single 5.13. Expect a steep, technical, gym-like feel to the holds. The older hardware is described as questionable, so inspect bolts and anchors before trusting them. Not a place for beginners.

ca_dog_pile_the.blurb: A pair of very large boulders high on the northwest hillside of the Santee Boulders in southern San Diego County, with problems around their bases and short roped lines on the faces. The mix is unusual: seven boulder problems, two top-rope lines, two trad routes and one sport route. Boulder grades run from the easiest up to a couple of very hard test pieces, while the roped climbs sit mostly between 5.8 and 5.10 with two much harder at 5.12. The two easier-grade faces are the favourites for newcomers.

ca_4_the_shock_block.blurb: The square block at the foot of a big scooped headwall in the Table Rock section of the Palisades on Mount St. Helena, in Wine Country north of the Bay. All twelve routes are bolted, and half of them sit in the 5.10 range, with two 5.11s, three 5.12s and one harder line at the top end. A few climbs run to two or three pitches. The routes have a reputation for being better than the block's modest look suggests. Hold off a couple of days after heavy rain, since the stone in this area can be soft.
